Yeah, shame on Asian parents for telling it straight and setting their kids up for success, right?

Many immigrant Asian parents raise their kids in poverty. As we all know it’s extremely hard to move socioeconomic classes, meaning if you are a kid raised in poverty, statistically there is a good chance you will live your entire life in poverty. But, the one way to defy the odds and take control of your socioeconomic destiny is to invest in your education and set yourself up on the right career path.

In this day and age of extreme income inequality, very few careers offer the chance at being something other than poor. We basically don’t have a middle class, anymore. You’re either poor or rich and the gap is widening in real time and shows no signs of stopping. I personally lament this, we’re a rich enough country to care for our poor people in much more empathetic ways such as single-payer healthcare and universal basic income, but there’s no political will to see these through. Meantime, you personally have to build a life. Are you going to be poor or are you going to be rich?

That’s a no brainer where the only remaining question is how to be rich and what rich means. In the last decade FAANG engineering has been hot, offering $200-300k first-year total comp to 21 year olds straight outta undergrad, $500k in mid-career (L5) and $1-2M after a decade or so of experience. Seems like a good deal but it’s actually a recipe to become a HENRY – High Earner, Not Rich Yet.

To be rich in the VHCOL places (otherwise known as places people actually want to live), the acronym you need to know is not FAANG but WLRK. They pay $500k to first year associates and $9m on average to partners. Partnership is achievable after a decade of billing >3,000 hours a year, which sounds like hell on earth, unless you were raised under stereotypical Asian parenting in which case that’s life as you have always known it.
